questions.q: What does enabling suspense posting allow?
options: Any journal can skip validation entirely
Journals can post to closed periods
Approval workflows are bypassed
An unbalanced journal can post anyway, with General Ledger automatically adding a balancing line against a designated suspense account
questions.explain: Suspense posting lets an out-of-balance journal post by automatically adding a balancing suspense line, rather than rejecting it.

questions.q: When does General Ledger use a source/category-specific suspense account instead of the default?
options: Never — only the default suspense account is ever used
Only for Manual-source journals
When the unbalanced journal's source and category match a specific pair that has its own dedicated suspense account
Only during year-end close
questions.explain: A specific source/category pair can have its own dedicated suspense account; otherwise the ledger's default is used.

questions.q: What does a non-zero suspense account balance actually represent?
options: A fully resolved transaction that needs no further attention
A real discrepancy that hasn't been explained or fixed yet
Extra cash the company can use freely
A budget variance
questions.explain: A suspense balance flags an unexplained discrepancy, not a resolved transaction.

questions.q: Why is a growing, unexplained suspense balance considered an audit red flag?
options: Because it suggests unbalanced entries are being routinely waved through rather than understood and fixed at the source
Because suspense accounts are illegal
Because it means the ledger's currency is wrong
Because it indicates too many approvals
questions.explain: An accumulating suspense balance suggests discrepancies aren't being investigated, which raises audit concerns.

questions.q: What kind of discrepancy might legitimately trigger suspense posting on an interfaced journal?
options: A missing approval signature
An intentional duplicate entry
A small rounding or timing difference from an upstream system
A change in the ledger's chart of accounts
questions.explain: Suspense posting is typically used for small out-of-balance amounts caused by rounding or timing issues from interfaced sources.
